subject: Implementation sprint: SDK wiring, migration windows, retries & rate-smoothing
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightline.io>, Jared Bloom <jared@brightline.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Implementation sprint: SDK wiring, migration windows, retries & rate-smoothing

Hi Elena & Jared —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Per our call I want to propose a short, pragmatic sprint to get Brightline's staging integration through: SDK wiring + a single endpoint migration (staging -> prod), and guardrails for retries/timeouts and rate smoothing.

High-level proposed plan (3 working days):
- Day 1: SDK install + sample app (we provide sample snippets and quick tests)
- Day 2: Endpoint migration dry-run in staging, run load tests with rate-smoothing knobs
- Day 3: Cutover window for a low-traffic route + post-cutover checks and rollback plan

Please confirm availability for the week of July 6. Technical attachments: redwood-sdk-samples-v1.2.zip (samples), migration-window-slides.pdf (timeline).

Key asks for Brightline before Day 1:
- A staging API key and access to a small test tenant (ops@brightline.io)
- Expected 95th percentile request size for the route we migrate (tokens per request)
- Any existing client-side retry logic you want to keep (so we don't double-retry)

I'll loop in Viv (runtime) if we need a kernel/quantization recommendation. Vanessa — can you prep the rate-fence defaults and a short runbook for the devs?

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks Tessa — July 6 works for our team for an initial kickoff (short sync). Quick answers to your asks:
- Staging API key: I'll have ops@brightline.io create a key and share by EOD today.
- 95th pct tokens: ~1,100 tokens per request for the route.
- Current retry policy: client retries up to 2x with exponential backoff (initial 200ms). We prefer keeping client-side retry but want Redwood to be the primary failover.

Can you confirm the low-traffic route candidate? We were thinking the /invoices/notify webhook route — it gets ~15 TPS at peak (but low risk for cutover).

Elena
VP, Integrations — Brightline

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2026 07:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Implementation sprint: SDK wiring, migration windows, retries & rate-smoothing

Tessa — quick internal readout before we go live with the kickoff tomorrow.

Notes / runbook draft (internal):
- SDK wiring: provide PATCH snippet to inject API key via REDWOOD_API_KEY env var; include sample for Node (axios + stream) and Python (requests + streaming generator).
- Client retry coordination: since Brightline will keep 2x client retries, set server-side idempotency window to 8s for the route and apply token-aware dedupe so duplicate tokens within window are collapsed.
- Timeouts: server-side per-token soft timeout = 35ms, hard timeout = 3500ms. We'll advise client timeout ~3000ms to align with soft/hard.
- Rate-smoothing: start with token-based smoothing profile: bucket_size=1200, refill_rate=300 TPS-equivalent; that'll keep bursts under the 95th percentile. Config sample attached as rate-fence-config.yaml.
- Migration window: schedule 1-hour cutover at 02:00 UTC; plan includes 20m warmup, 20m monitored ramp, 20m full switch + quick rollback if error rate > 2%.

I've attached the YAML and a short Node/Python sample we can drop into the repo during Day 1. Vivek — are we comfortable with the dedupe latency on 1k tokens?

– Vanessa
Senior Implementation Engineer, Redwood

[attachment: rate-fence-config.yaml]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Implementation sprint: SDK wiring, migration windows, retries & rate-smoothing

Vanessa — quick technical confirmation:
- Dedupe window at 8s for 1.1k tokens is fine; KV cache checks add ~2ms median latency on our staging runtime with current kernel selection.
- Suggest we instrument a short synthetic that sends 50 concurrent 1.1k-token requests to staging during the warmup period to validate backpressure and memory usage.
- If memory spikes > 75% on the worker pool, fallback to a lighter quantized runtime variant for the route; ops can toggle via router policy.

I'll stand by during the cutover.

— Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood

From: Elena Morales <elena@brightline.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Bloom <jared@brightline.io>, ops@brightline.io
Date: Wed, 6 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Implementation sprint: SDK wiring, migration windows, retries & rate-smoothing

Appreciate the details — we got the attachments and the example snippets look straightforward. Confirming: we will
- Share staging API key by EOD today
- Stand up the synthetic load test you suggested for warmup (Jared will own)
- Schedule the 02:00 UTC cutover on July 10 (ops team confirmed low traffic)

One final ask: can Redwood add a short fallback policy to route traffic to the older model variant automatically if error rate > 1.5% for 3 continuous minutes? That would keep customer-facing impact minimal.

If you can add that to the runbook I'll mark this thread ready for Day 1.

Thanks —
Elena
